tagline: Two Piedmont peaks protected after a campaign against mineral excavation.
intro: Crowders Mountain Drive belongs to North Carolina’s scenic-byway system in the Piedmont. Its namesake rises nearly 800 feet above the surrounding terrain between Kings Mountain and Gastonia. Crowders Mountain and The Pinnacle have sheer cliffs 100–150 feet high.

In the early 1970s, mineral exploration prompted citizens, educational institutions and local governments to press for protection. North Carolina created the state park in 1973; Crowders Mountain itself joined it in 1978 and The Pinnacle in 1987.

Kings Mountain lies west of Charlotte along I-85. Within the nearby park, Crowders Mountain occupies the northeastern section and The Pinnacle the western section. The summit views require a hike: trails lead to both peaks, with Charlotte’s towers visible on a clear day.

moments.title: Kings Mountain
moments.text: Kings Mountain took its name from a battlefield across the state line. The settlement had been called White Plains before its incorporation and name change in 1874. Downtown’s local history museum occupies a former post office built in 1940 with Depression-era works funding. Postal use ended in 1986. The city acquired the building in 2000 and leased it to the historical society for a museum. The museum building is Colonial Revival in style. Elsewhere downtown, the Mauney Memorial Library and two historic bridges are among the city’s National Register properties.

moments.title: Crowders Mountain
moments.text: Crowders Mountain was once a prospect for mineral excavation. Exploratory sampling in the early 1970s targeted ground along what is now the Backside Trail. Local citizens, educational institutions and governments responded by pressing the state to protect the area. The mountain became part of the park in 1978. Its summit also has a separate history of communications: WGNC-FM erected a tower in the late 1940s, and three radio towers occupy a privately owned summit plot. The towers relay more than commercial radio: wireless phone companies, railroads and local emergency services also use them to carry signals.

moments.title: The Pinnacle
moments.text: At 1,705 feet, The Pinnacle is the highest point in Gaston County. It is the remnant of a quartzite ridge formed approximately 400–500 million years ago. Softer material that once surrounded and covered it has gradually worn away. The peak belongs to the Kings Mountain Belt, a string of monadnocks and rock types extending through the Carolina Piedmont. A hiking trail reaches the summit, where views can extend west and north to the Blue Ridge and east toward Charlotte. Many other formations in the belt can also be seen from the summit, placing this isolated peak within a longer chain.
